discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 021931 CCA
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
230 PM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Some patchy drizzle or light rain showers/sprinkles will likely 
  continue at times through this evening.

- Much better chances for rain (80-100%) arrive late Tuesday
  night into early Wednesday. Rainfall amounts are generally 
  expected to be one quarter of an inch or less.

- Highs will be well into the 70s on Tuesday with breezy
  conditions but otherwise highs remain around 60 the rest of
  the week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 225 PM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

Broad advective forcing continues across the region with water vapor 
imagery and near term hi-res guidance initializations depicting
next weak short wave across the Mid MS Valley. THis should 
allow for a few more waves of drizzle and possibly a few light 
rain showers this evening but most locations will be dry or 
experience just trace amounts. As mentioned in previous 
discussion, guidance has struggled today with temps with a 
maintenance in blended guidance of a warm bias. Extensive low 
clouds and occasional very light drizzle have resulted in 
temperatures hovering from the 55 to 60 degree range for most 
locations. Temperatures are expected to show little movement 
through the night tonight as warm advection offsets most of 
diurnal tendencies. Overnight, the aforementioned lead short 
wave should shift east of the area allowing for mid/upper level 
height rises to build back in from the west.

The attention for Tuesday will be on evolution of large scale 
upper trough, and in particular the upper height minimum across 
the southern Plains that will lift north as an upper jet streak 
progresses through the downstream portion of this trough. 
Moisture transport will steadily increase in advance of this 
trough tonight into Tuesday, but with better mid/upper dynamics 
displaced well west/southwest, will maintain a dry forecast 
through the day. Windy and warm conditions will be the main 
story on Tuesday as near term buffer soundings suggest some 
potential of tapping into 30 to 35 knot top of boundary layer 
flow across northwest/portions of north central Indiana during 
the afternoon hours. Thickening mid cloud and moistening low/mid
levels could result in mixing heights not being maximized 
however. Based on magnitude of low level thermals alone, highs 
should approach record levels in the middle 70s for Tuesday.

Categorical PoPs have been maintained for Tuesday night into
Wednesday AM due to the combination of initial LLJ forcing 
followed by passage of cold front. While cannot completely rule 
out an isolated storm with some very weak elevated instability 
Tuesday night, any instability of note will likely be confined 
well south across the Lower MS Valley. With stronger upper 
dynamics expected to bypass the area to the southwest/south, 
frontal convergence fields are a bit weaker across the local 
area with a camp of guidance still suggesting more limited 
rainfall amounts. Given progressive nature of LLJ axis and low 
level baroclinic zone, this does not look to be a significant 
hydro event.

Dry slot punches into the area from southwest to northeast on 
Wednesday, withs some additional rain showers possible 
Thursday night through Friday as better moisture profiles wrap 
around the slowly eastward meandering upper low. Some lake 
enhancement is expected with the rain showers, but instability 
depths are quite limited without any push of dramatically colder
mid level air.

The large scale pattern will favor additional influence from an 
eastern Pacific jet streak in closing off another system across
central CONUS for the weekend but confidence in timing these 
additional rain chances is low. Given expected weak 
baroclinicity in this pattern and preference to systems more
vertically stacked in nature, no significant rainfall events 
are anticipated through the next 7 days. Temperatures should 
trend near normal by this weekend into early next week.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z TUESDAY/...
Issued at 1222 PM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

Southerly flow through the period with winds 10-12kt through the
afternoon. MVFR ceilings with occasional light drizzle will 
give way to a occasional light rain showers into the evening 
hours, especially near FWA. Low-level wind shear will spread 
across the area tonight after 06-07Z with a shear vector of 
200-210 degrees. LLWS will subside after 13-15Z Tue, but expect
southerly winds to increase and become gusty up to 25kt during
peak heating.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory from 7 AM Tuesday to 7 AM EST Wednesday 
     for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

spc.summary: Severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts, hail, and a few tornadoes are expected across parts of the southern and central Plains from this afternoon into tonight.
spc.text:
SPC AC 022002

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0202 PM CST Mon Nov 02 2026

   Valid 022000Z - 031200Z

   ...THERE IS AN ENHANCED RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS
   NORTH-CENTRAL OKLAHOMA AND SOUTH-CENTRAL KANSAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts, hail, and a few
   tornadoes are expected across parts of the southern and central
   Plains from this afternoon into tonight.

   ...20Z Update...
   A potent shortwave trough evident in water vapor satellite imagery
   is beginning to take on a neutral-to-negative tilt, as the trough
   and its associated jet streak progresses eastward out of New Mexico
   into the Texas Panhandle. In advance of this shortwave, deepening
   cumulus and thunderstorm development in response to the approaching
   wave are evident on visible satellite and radar imagery. As better
   moisture is transported northward ahead of this development and a
   narrow corridor of mixing further destabilizes the environment,
   these (and subsequent) thunderstorms are expected to become severe.
   Storms should initially favor a supercell mode before growing
   upscale into linear convective complexes. 

   The Enhanced Risk for tornadoes was expanded south and west into
   portions of Central Oklahoma to account for recent observational
   trends and short-term forecast guidance, while hail probabilities
   were expanded further north and east to account for ongoing elevated
   convection capable of 1.00-1.50 inch hail. Greater uncertainty
   exists in where the primary corridor of damaging wind potential will
   materialize, but leading edge bowing segments will be capable of
   65-80 MPH damaging wind gusts.

   ..Halbert-K.. 11/02/2026

   .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1006 AM CST Mon Nov 02 2026/

   ...Central/Southern Plains...
   A large upper trough is present today over the western states, with
   a strong shortwave trough rotating across the Four-Corners area. As
   this features and its associated 80+ knot mid level jet begin to
   eject into the southern Plains this afternoon, numerous
   thunderstorms are expected to form from west-central TX northward
   into parts of KS/NE.  Widespread dewpoints in the low-mid 60s,
   pockets of heating, and strong low-level winds across a broad area
   will result in conditional risks of damaging winds, a few tornadoes,
   and some hail.  However, there are a few specific scenarios that
   appear most likely to focus that risk.

   ...OK/KS early this afternoon...
   Water vapor imagery shows a lead trough currently moving into
   western OK.  This feature is expected to aid in the development of
   scattered thunderstorms by early afternoon, tracking into southern
   KS.  Wind fields are very strong in this area, and a few supercell
   structures are expected.  However, forecast soundings show poor
   low-level thermodynamics with LFC heights around 700mb.  This should
   limit the severe risk.

   ...KS/OK/North TX this afternoon/evening...
   The primary severe risk will be with storms forming along the
   surface dryline over western OK and south-central KS by late
   afternoon.  These storms will also be in a favorable shear profile
   for supercell structures, but cooling temperatures aloft will also
   increase the risk of robust updrafts as storms track quickly
   northeastward.  Damaging winds and a few tornadoes are the main
   concerns.  By early evening, the Pacific cold front will catch up to
   the convective line, resulting in more linear structures and greater
   wind potential.

   ...West-Central TX...
   The aforementioned convective line will build southward into
   west-central TX through the evening, with some risk of damaging
   winds and a tornado or two.  Low-level winds and large-scale
   dynamics will be weaker with southward extent, lessening the overall
   severe threat.

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0100Z

spc.summary: Scattered storms will occur from the Sabine and Lower Mississippi Valleys northward into the Mid Mississippi Valley on Tuesday. A few thunderstorms may produce damaging gusts and a couple of tornadoes.
spc.text:
SPC AC 021727

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1127 AM CST Mon Nov 02 2026

   Valid 031200Z - 041200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM EAST TEXAS
   AND THE ARK-LA-MISS TO THE MID MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Scattered storms will occur from the Sabine and Lower Mississippi
   Valleys northward into the Mid Mississippi Valley on Tuesday. A few
   thunderstorms may produce damaging gusts and a couple of tornadoes.

   ...MS Valley area...
   The primary surface cyclone is expected to develop
   north-northeastward from eastern KS Tuesday morning to the upper MS
   Valley by Wednesday morning, as the associated midlevel trough
   progresses eastward and northeastward across the MS Valley well in
   advance of an upstream trough approaching northern CA.  An
   associated surface cold front will likewise move eastward through
   the day across MO/AR.  Clouds and convection will be relatively
   widespread along the front at the beginning of the period, and a
   messy/QLCS convective mode will likely persist through the day.

   The primary cyclone developing away from the moisture source region,
   the widespread clouds/rain, and poor midlevel lapse all suggest that
   warm sector buoyancy will also remain limited through the period. 
   The richer low-level moisture and slightly larger buoyancy will
   likely remain confined to the Ark-La-Miss, where low-level
   shear/hodograph curvature is forecast to be sufficient for embedded
   rotating storms capable of producing a tornado or two and isolated
   wind damage.  The isolated severe threat could persist into Tuesday
   night across northern MS and vicinity on the east edge of the
   returning low-level moisture and near the southern extent of the
   stronger low-level flow/shear.  Farther north into the mid MS
   Valley, the severe threat farther north will be confined to the
   strongest embedded line segments during the day.  There is a small
   chance for low-topped supercells near the surface cyclone Tuesday
   afternoon.

   ..Thompson.. 11/02/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.summary: Severe storms are unlikely on Wednesday.
spc.text:
SPC AC 021927

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0127 PM CST Mon Nov 02 2026

   Valid 041200Z - 051200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely on Wednesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A cyclone is forecast to occlude in the vicinity of WI as a cold
   front slows its eastward movement late in the period across the
   upper OH Valley, and stalls across the TN/lower MS Valley region. 
   The southern extent of an associated midlevel trough will brush the
   northern edge of a weakly unstable warm sector early in the period. 
   Forcing for ascent and low-level flow/shear will tend to weaken
   within the warm sector by afternoon, so any threat for severe storms
   in the vicinity of northern AL appears too marginal for an outlook
   area.  Otherwise, isolated lightning flashes will be possible into
   parts of the Great Lakes with marginal buoyancy.

   Farther west, a shortwave trough will progress quickly eastward over
   the Four Corners to the southern High Plains late in the period. 
   Ascent in the left-exit region of the mid-upper jet streak, in
   combination with sufficient moisture and steep lapse rates, will
   support the potential for lightning flashes with low-topped
   convection.

   ..Thompson.. 11/02/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 3 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0830Z

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
